items.title: US defence secretary Hegseth meets Netanyahu on unannounced Israel visit
items.why: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at an air base in southern Israel on Monday, Axios and Israeli media report; the Pentagon declined to comment. Netanyahu later released video of a call in which he told President Trump they have 'a job to finish'.
items.matters: It came a day after Trump endorsed Netanyahu for Israel's 27 October election and as Russia's foreign minister visited Tehran.

items.title: Super Typhoon Champi enters Philippine waters; storm signals raised in northern Luzon
items.why: Champi, named Rosal locally, entered the Philippine area of responsibility at 02:40 UTC on Tuesday with winds of 185 km/h, the weather agency PAGASA says. Signal No. 1 is up in Batanes and parts of Cagayan, Isabela and Catanduanes. PAGASA expects it to leave Philippine waters by early Saturday.
items.matters: Taiwan's weather agency expects Champi to turn north on Thursday but bring heavy rain to northern and eastern Taiwan from Friday.

items.title: South Korean shares fall 3.7% as AI doubts hit Asian tech stocks
items.why: Seoul's KOSPI index closed 3.73% lower at 5,552.74 on Tuesday 20 October, with SK hynix down 4.2% and Samsung Electronics down 3%. Shares in Tokyo and Hong Kong also fell, AFP reports, as investors questioned whether heavy spending on AI will pay off.
items.matters: Meta and Tesla report results this week, which investors will watch for signs that AI spending is earning returns.

items.title: US judge orders ex-OpenAI engineer held without bail in recording-device case
items.why: A US federal judge in San Francisco on Monday ordered Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi former OpenAI engineer, held until trial, citing a 'significant' flight risk. He is charged with hiding a recording device in an OpenAI meeting room. Prosecutors cite help from Saudi officials; his lawyer denies he would flee.
items.matters: Prosecutors call the case a national security concern; the next hearing is on 6 November.

items.title: Japan launches probe to bring back samples from Mars moon Phobos
items.why: Japan's space agency JAXA launched its MMX probe on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima at 19:41 UTC on 19 October (04:41 Tuesday, Japan time). About 71 minutes later it was released into its planned orbit, Jiji Press reports. MMX should reach Mars in 2027 and return samples in 2031.
items.matters: No mission has yet brought back material from the Mars system; it may show how Mars's two small moons formed.

items.title: Portugal federation bans Ronaldo for 30 days over squad walkout
items.why: Portugal's football federation suspended captain Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, for 30 days and fined him €255 on 19 October for leaving the national team camp in Copenhagen after a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus. Reports say the ban is backdated to the start of October.
items.matters: He is expected to be available for Portugal's Nations League games in November if Jesus picks him.

items.title: Trump orders new women's health division at US National Institutes of Health
items.why: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Monday telling health officials to set up a women's health division at the National Institutes of Health within 90 days, plus a White House task force. First Lady Melania Trump led the effort; the order names no specific funding.
items.matters: Critics cited by Al Jazeera question how it will work after thousands of NIH staff were laid off and budgets cut.

items.title: US orders civilian government agencies to stop using China's DeepSeek AI
items.why: The US Department of Homeland Security has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove AI tools from Chinese company DeepSeek, including other firms' products built on its models. The order, made public on 19 October, does not cover the military, AFP reports.
items.matters: DHS says using the tools may send sensitive data to China; the two countries' leaders are due to meet next month.

items.title: Saudi Arabia postpones its 'Davos in the Desert' investment summit to 2027
items.why: The Future Investment Initiative, due in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from 26 to 29 October, has been moved to 2027, organisers said on Monday. AFP and Reuters link the delay to Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, including on Riyadh's main airport. New dates have not been set.
items.matters: Expected speakers included the heads of BlackRock, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan; two other Saudi business events were also postponed.

items.title: Drone strikes across Sudan reported to kill more than 160 people
items.why: A drone strike near a market in Al-Dibab, in RSF-held West Kordofan, killed about 80 people on Sunday evening, a medical source and a witness told AFP; the RSF's administration blamed the army. Medics and rights groups say drone attacks killed more than 160 people in recent days.
items.matters: Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have fought since April 2023; the UN says it condemns the strikes 'unequivocally'.

items.title: Pakistan confirms first polio case in Karachi since December 2024
items.why: Pakistan's polio programme confirmed on Monday that a six-month-old boy in Karachi East has wild poliovirus, the country's seventh case this year and Karachi's first since December 2024. Five of the seven cases are in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province and two in Sindh, which includes Karachi.
items.matters: A vaccination campaign from 2 to 8 November aims to reach nearly 24 million children under five in 97 districts.

items.title: Ruling on Senegal's Africa Cup of Nations appeal expected in late November
items.why: The Court of Arbitration for Sport said on 19 October it will rule on Senegal's appeal at the end of November, not within days as first signalled. Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in January's final, but African football's governing body, CAF, later awarded Morocco the title.
items.matters: CAF ruled Senegal forfeited by walking off for 14 minutes in protest at a penalty; Senegal says the referee let play finish.

items.title: Benny Gantz quits Israel's election race eight days before the vote
items.why: Former army chief Benny Gantz said on Monday he will not run in Israel's 27 October election, after polls repeatedly put his Blue and White party below the 3.25% threshold needed to enter parliament. 'The responsibility is mine,' he said. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot called it a 'responsible' decision.
items.matters: Gantz was Netanyahu's main rival in three elections; his party's name will still appear on the ballot.

items.title: Europe's Euclid space telescope finds its first new comet
items.why: The European Space Agency says Euclid, built to map distant galaxies, has found a previously unknown comet, C/2026 S1 (Euclid), about 1.3 billion km from Earth. A University of Helsinki PhD student spotted it in September images; the Minor Planet Center confirmed it on 8 October.
items.matters: It suggests survey telescopes can spot comets far from the Sun, early enough for missions such as ESA's planned Comet Interceptor.

items.title: Exiled critic of Rwanda's President Kagame found killed in Uganda
items.why: A former Rwandan army sergeant who ran a popular YouTube channel criticising President Paul Kagame was found dead on 17 October in Mpigi district, near Uganda's capital, Kampala. Ugandan police said on Monday they had opened a murder case; no one has been arrested.
items.matters: Rwanda's government has not commented; Al Jazeera notes Rwandan authorities have been accused before of killing opponents abroad.

items.changed: Updated: death toll rises to at least 53; Saudi Arabia postpones its big Riyadh investment summit to 2027
items.title: Yemen officials say Houthi missiles killed at least 53 at army camp
items.why: Houthi ballistic missiles hit a government army training camp near Ataq, in Shabwa province, southern Yemen, on Monday. Yemeni military officials say at least 53 soldiers were killed and about 200 recruits wounded. The Houthis say Saudi officers ran the camp, without giving evidence.
items.matters: Saudi Arabia has postponed its Future Investment Initiative summit, due in Riyadh next week, to 2027 after Houthi strikes.

items.title: Baby orangutan rescued from a flat near Mumbai returns to Indonesia
items.why: A young male Sumatran orangutan, found in an apartment in Thane, near Mumbai, India, in November 2024, was flown to Medan, Indonesia, on 19 October. He will go to a rescue centre in North Sumatra to learn climbing and foraging before any release, Indonesian officials say.
items.matters: India waived the cost of his care; five more young orangutans found in India's Odisha state in September may follow.

items.title: Bangladesh measles outbreak deaths pass 1,200, health officials say
items.why: Five more children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours to Monday morning, Bangladesh's health directorate says, taking this year's toll to 1,201: 104 confirmed and 1,097 suspected. It has recorded 214,551 suspected cases since mid-March.
items.matters: Health experts blame gaps in childhood vaccination and weak infection control, The Daily Star reports.

items.title: Kenyan court convicts cult leader Paul Mackenzie over 191 starvation deaths
items.why: A Kenyan court on Monday found pastor Paul Mackenzie and 28 others guilty of murdering 191 people, 190 of them children. Prosecutors said he told followers to starve themselves to 'meet Jesus' in Shakahola forest, on Kenya's coast. Sentencing is set for 6 November.
items.matters: Authorities say more than 400 people died in the forest; Mackenzie also faces separate terrorism and manslaughter charges.

items.title: Twelve migrants, including a baby, die off Greek islands
items.why: Six people died off Lesbos when a speedboat carrying migrants hit a Greek coast guard vessel and capsized, and six more died when another speedboat overturned north of Samos, Greece's coast guard says. Two survivors were arrested on suspicion of smuggling.
items.matters: Greece's government blames smugglers; officials say the exact cause of the Lesbos collision is under investigation.

items.title: Floods from Storm Adam kill at least four in eastern Spain
items.why: Torrential rain flooded towns in Spain's Valencia region on Monday, with up to 700 litres per square metre in 24 hours in places, AFP reports. Officials say three people died in Valencia and one in Catalonia; more than 400 were rescued and over 2,000 evacuated, mostly in Oliva.
items.matters: About 800,000 people were told to stay indoors on Monday; floods in the same region killed more than 230 people in 2024.

items.title: Louvre closes for the day as students block its entrances
items.why: About 50 students, mostly from the École du Louvre art school, blocked the entrances of the Louvre in Paris on 19 October, and the museum stayed shut all day, its management said. They were backing France's school protest movement and denouncing what they called police repression.
items.matters: The Louvre, the world's most visited museum, says visitors who had booked will be refunded automatically.

items.title: China to require export licences for tunnel boring machines from 18 November
items.why: China's commerce ministry said on Monday 19 October that exporters of tunnel boring machines and their key parts will need a licence from 18 November. It cited national security and the machines' military as well as civilian uses. Walking excavators and some dredger parts are also covered.
items.matters: India, which is building metros and rail tunnels, relies heavily on imported boring machines, Reuters and PTI report.

items.changed: Updated: shares rebound about 4% on Tuesday morning after the exchange tightened limits on daily falls
items.title: Indonesian shares rebound after two-day slump over MSCI downgrade warning
items.why: Jakarta's main share index was up about 4% at 5,205 at midday on Tuesday 20 October, after falling nearly 15% over Friday and Monday when MSCI warned it may move Indonesia to 'standalone' status. The stock exchange has halved its daily limit on share-price falls to 7%.
items.matters: Bank Indonesia sets interest rates on Wednesday; some economists expect a rise to support the rupiah, which is near its record low.

items.title: Elon Musk pledges one SpaceX share to every child in America
items.why: Elon Musk said on X on Monday that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to 'every kid in America'. With more than 70 million under-18s and Friday's closing price of $146, that would be worth over $10 billion. He gave no details.
items.matters: Musk made the pledge in reply to Anthropic's plan to put 5% of its shares into a public benefit fund.

items.title: UN food agency cuts aid to half a million people in Gaza
items.why: The UN World Food Programme said on Monday it will stop monthly food aid for about 500,000 people in Gaza because of a funding shortfall, cutting its caseload from 1.6 million to 1.1 million. It says about two-thirds of Gazans are acutely food insecure.
items.matters: The WFP blames lower donor funding as winter nears; Israel's military aid body, COGAT, says Gaza is well supplied.

items.changed: Updated: Australian media report she has lost a leg; police call it an isolated incident and no charges have yet been laid
items.title: Australian MP Helen Haines critically injured after being hit by car
items.why: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was hit by a four-wheel drive outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday afternoon. She remains in a critical condition in a Melbourne hospital; Australian media report she has lost a leg. A 43-year-old man is in custody but has not yet been charged.
items.matters: Federal police call it an 'isolated incident' with no known further threats; they say charges could include harming a Commonwealth official.

items.title: Zelensky accuses US of holding back Patriot missiles Europe has paid for
items.why: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday the US is delaying Patriot air-defence interceptors that European allies have already paid for, and that the shipment awaits Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's approval. Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied the US had cut intelligence sharing with Kyiv.
items.matters: Trump said Zelensky 'doesn't know what he's talking about' and said he is open to meeting Putin and Xi.

items.title: China's economy grows 4.5% in third quarter, slightly beating forecasts
items.why: China's economy grew 4.5% year on year in July–September, official figures showed on Monday, up from 4.3% in the previous quarter and just above the 4.4% economists expected. Retail sales rose 1.1% in September, while investment in property development fell 20.6% in the first nine months.
items.matters: Growth relies on strong exports while shoppers stay cautious, which matters for the many countries that trade with China.

items.changed: Updated: the Rays won Game 6 7-3 to take the series 4-2 and will meet the Brewers in the World Series
items.title: Rays beat Guardians to reach World Series against Brewers
items.why: The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in St Petersburg, Florida, on 19 October to win the American League Championship Series 4-2. Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz hit two-run home runs; pitcher Freddy Peralta was named series MVP.
items.matters: Neither the Rays nor the Milwaukee Brewers has ever won the World Series, which starts in Milwaukee on 23 October.

items.title: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro trade insults in first Brazil run-off debate
items.why: Brazil's President Lula and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro met on Sunday night in São Paulo for their first debate before the 25 October run-off. They accused each other of corruption and clashed over security, healthcare and the economy. AFP says two polls this week put Bolsonaro ahead 51% to 49%.
items.matters: The winner will lead Latin America's largest country; a second and final TV debate is scheduled for Friday 23 October.

items.title: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund
items.why: US AI company Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, said on 18 October it will put 5% of its shares into a new fund for public-good projects, subject to shareholder approval. Its board may add 2% for every 50% rise in the company's value.
items.matters: Anthropic says the fund could support people affected by AI-driven job changes; it cannot be used for lobbying or political donations.

items.title: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case as Congo outbreak reaches new province
items.why: Kenya's health ministry confirmed an eighth Ebola case on Sunday: a 49-year-old man who worked as an attendant near the country's first patient and was already in quarantine. Congo says the virus has reached an eighth province, North Ubangi, bordering the Central African Republic.
items.matters: The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment; Congo's latest report counts 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths, Reuters says.

items.title: Elizabeth Holmes documentary takes $15 million in surprise box-office debut
items.why: You Can See Everything, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's nearly three-hour film about the jailed Theranos founder, took about $15 million in North America over 16–18 October from just 855 cinemas, studio estimates show. The video-game film Street Fighter topped the chart with $31 million.
items.matters: Screen Daily calls it the biggest documentary debut since Fahrenheit 9/11 in 2004, leaving aside concert films.

items.title: UN nature summit opens in Armenia with most targets off track
items.why: Nearly 200 countries are meeting in Armenia's capital, Yerevan, for two weeks of UN biodiversity talks, COP17, the first review of a 2022 pact to halt nature loss by 2030. Opening the conference, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said countries are "not yet on track".
items.matters: A UN report says current plans would protect only 26% of land and 12% of oceans by 2030, against a 30% goal.

items.changed: Updated: Mumbai Police say none of the three suspects is a minor; police are examining an unverified claim of responsibility
items.title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff unhurt after gunmen fire at his car
items.why: Gunmen fired at actor Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area, India, on 18 October, police say. He was unhurt; his driver and a bystander were injured. Mumbai Police say none of the three suspects arrested in Kota, Rajasthan, is a minor: one is 18, two are 22.
items.matters: Police are examining an unverified claim of responsibility by a gangster linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang; no weapon has been found.

items.title: Sergei Loznitsa's Soviet-era documentary Imperium wins top London Film Festival prize
items.why: Imperium, a 175-minute documentary built from footage Italian cameramen shot in the Soviet Union in the early 1970s, won Best Film at the BFI London Film Festival on 18 October. Thailand's 9 Temples to Heaven won the best first feature award.
items.matters: Concrete Land, about a family facing displacement in Jordan, won the festival's documentary prize, the Grierson Award.

items.title: Dozens of orangutans rescued from Indonesia's fires on Borneo
items.why: At least 51 critically endangered orangutans have been rescued from burning forest in West Kalimantan, on Borneo, since early August, the conservation agency and the charity YIARI say. Many were thin and stressed; 27 need further care. Indonesia's forestry ministry suggests up to 96 across Kalimantan.
items.matters: Satellite images show fire damaged over 90% of a protected forest area where many were found, Antara reports.

items.title: Ethiopians win both Amsterdam Marathon races; Diriba sets women's course record
items.why: Buze Diriba won the women's race in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, on 18 October in 2:16:12, 40 seconds inside the course record, World Athletics says. Fellow Ethiopian Lemi Berhanu won the men's race in 2:03:33, three seconds outside the record.
items.matters: Diriba's run, in wet conditions, moves her to 16th on the world all-time list, World Athletics says.

items.changed: Updated: a Bogotá court ordered the museum to preserve the removed works and remove no others, pending a full ruling
items.title: Colombian court orders National Museum to keep works the government removed
items.why: A Bogotá family court on 19 October ordered Colombia's National Museum to keep the works the Culture Ministry removed, and to take down no others, pending a full ruling. At least 30 pieces on feminism, LGBTQ rights and the 2016 peace deal had been removed.
items.matters: The government says museums must not be instruments of 'political indoctrination'; riot police broke up a protest at the museum on Saturday.

items.changed: Updated: a Russian drone strike on a park in Kharkiv region killed six people, including two children, officials say
items.title: Russian drone kills six in Kharkiv park as strikes cut Ukraine's power
items.why: Russia struck 28 energy facilities in 11 Ukrainian regions overnight into Monday, cutting power to at least 550,000 households, President Zelensky says. On Monday afternoon a Russian drone hit a park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv region, killing six people, including two girls, the regional governor says.
items.matters: Both sides are striking energy sites despite the 'energy ceasefire' US President Donald Trump announced on 11 October.

items.changed: Updated: Lavrov called the US-Israeli attacks illegal; Iran's president says Tehran will not accept demands imposed by force
items.title: Russia's Lavrov calls US-Israeli attacks on Iran illegal during Tehran visit
items.why: On his first visit to Iran since the war began, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov called the US and Israeli attacks illegal and said Moscow wants to prevent a return to large-scale war. President Pezeshkian said Iran rejects demands imposed by force but will settle disputes through dialogue.
items.matters: UKMTO says 10 ships were attacked near Hormuz last week; Iran says the strait would reopen if the US lifts its blockade.

items.changed: Updated: curfews in Paris, Lyon, Nice, Lille and Bordeaux on Monday night; the prime minister says they helped keep the night calm
items.title: France's local curfews help keep night calm, prime minister says
items.why: Partial overnight curfews took effect on Monday in parts of Paris, Lyon, Bordeaux, Nice and Lille after a weekend of riots and looting. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said they 'helped keep the night calm' and more would follow where needed; police reported no major incidents.
items.matters: Officials estimate at least 3,000 businesses were hit; Macron refused his interior minister's resignation and ordered a review of policing failures.

items.changed: Updated: Brent steady near $110 on Tuesday; Yemen's Houthis claim strikes on Saudi oil sites, unconfirmed
items.title: Oil holds near five-month high as Gulf attacks offset Russia sanctions waiver
items.why: Brent crude was steady at about $109.70 a barrel early on Tuesday 20 October, near Friday's five-month high of $110. Traders are weighing a US waiver of some Russia sanctions against attacks on ships near Hormuz and unconfirmed Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi oil sites.
items.matters: Prices remain well above pre-war levels, keeping pressure on fuel, transport and food costs.
